answer_text: Textbooks often use case studies to illustrate this kind of geographic concept. This is a foundational concept in geography. A delta is a landform created when a river deposits sediment as it flows into a larger body of water, such as an ocean or lake, causing the river to split into multiple smaller channels. The Nile Delta in Egypt is a well-known example. This topic connects to several other physical geography concepts covered in the same unit.
